description: Build the DynamoDB single-table driver (table <DYNAMODB_TABLE_PREFIX>App, keys PK/SK, one overloaded GSI1) behind the FEAT-001 interfaces, plus its default-suite unit tests. A fake client is used, so no Docker is needed. This is plan.md items 7-8 and design.md sections 5.1-5.10, 3.3 and 8.3 (items.test and commands.test rows), with [F34] (key guard lower bound 1) and [P1] (throwOnRequestTimeout: true). It adds @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb and @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb ^3.1162.0; repositories/dynamodb/{client,keys,items,ops,links,tableDefinition,index}.ts; nine repository files; and the registry's dynamodb branch, which replaces the FEAT-001 placeholder. Running against DynamoDB Local is FEAT-004. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: With no node process from the worktree running (EBUSY risk on better-sqlite3), run in C:\Antigravity\Urbani DPI\.worktrees\dpi2: `npm install @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb@^3.1162.0 @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb@^3.1162.0 --workspace @urbani/backend`. Both packages share one version. Only packages/backend/package.json and the root package-lock.json may change.

Create packages/backend/src/repositories/dynamodb/client.ts: DynamoContext { client, doc: Pick<DynamoDBDocumentClient,'send'>, tableName, destroy() } and createDynamoContext({ region, endpoint, tableName }) per design §5.10. Use maxAttempts 3 and requestHandler { connectionTimeout: 2_000, requestTimeout: 5_000, throwOnRequestTimeout: true } [P1]. Use dummy credentials { accessKeyId: 'local', secretAccessKey: 'local' } ONLY when endpoint is set; otherwise rely on the default credential chain. marshallOptions.removeUndefinedValues true; unmarshallOptions.wrapNumbers false.

Create dynamodb/keys.ts: key builders for every §5.2 row (ROLE, USER, USER_EMAIL, PREFS, AUDIT ts#id with GSI1 ACTOR#, ALERT with GSI1 ALERTSRC#, SERVICE, ENVIRONMENT, LOG/METRIC/AI_ANALYSIS with sparse ALERTLINK# GSI1PK and typed GSI1SK, USAGE date#modelId, INTEGRATION, CHAT#<sid> SESSION/MSG#/FEEDBACK#, CHATUSER# GSI1, HEALTH/PING), ENTITY_TYPES (exactly the 16 values) and fitsKey(pk, sk): 1 <= utf8Bytes(pk) <= 2048 and 1 <= utf8Bytes(sk) <= 1024 [F34].

Create dynamodb/items.ts: the 16 builders named in the §5.4 rule (roleItem, userItem, emailLockItem, preferencesItem, auditItem, alertItem, serviceItem, environmentItem, logItem, metricItem, usageItem, analysisItem, integrationItem, chatSessionItem, chatMessageItem, feedbackItem). Each sets entityType and checks every key attribute (PK, SK, GSI1PK, GSI1SK) with the [F34] bounds, throwing PersistenceError INVALID_ARGUMENT. Add item->record mappers that emit exactly the SQLite mappers' keys with null where absent; users map to snake_case UserRow with is_active: isActive ? 1 : 0, and audit query items have no `result`. Add budgetEvidence (EVIDENCE_BUDGET_BYTES = 256*1024, whole trailing lines dropped, warn { alertId, keptLines, droppedLines }) and assertItemSize (ITEM_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES = 380*1024 -> ITEM_TOO_LARGE) per §5.8.

Create dynamodb/ops.ts, the ONLY module importing QueryCommand, BatchGetCommand and BatchWriteCommand. It holds send(ctx, command, op, opts?) applying translateAwsError (the §5.10 table, fatal flags and hints; logs op/awsError/requestId only, never item contents), queryAll, queryCount, queryUpTo, batchGetAll and batchWriteAll with the §5.7 signatures (chunks 100/25; up to 5 retries with 50ms*2^n backoff plus jitter, then UNAVAILABLE), and mapLimit(items, 8, fn). Create dynamodb/links.ts with unlinkAll(ctx, alertId) per §5.4, and dynamodb/tableDefinition.ts with APP_TABLE_GSI1 = 'GSI1' and buildCreateTableInput(tableName) per §9.5, with a comment pointing at infra/lib/persistence-construct.ts.

Create dynamodb/{alert,telemetry,user,preferences,ai,audit,integration,chat,health}Repository.ts implementing the §5.3 access patterns (1-47; 7 not implemented) with the §5.4 algorithms. Rules: #name/:value placeholders everywhere; attribute_exists(#pk) on every update that mirrors a SQL UPDATE; #entityType in the SET of upsertLivePreservingStatus, preferences.update (plus #userId) and setFeedback; the live-upsert SET list generated from items.alertItem(alert,'LIVE','OPEN') minus PK/SK/status/ack attributes, plus #status = if_not_exists(#status, :open); upsertUser follows the §5.4 decision table with at most 2 attempts plus the inconsistent-lock send; findByEmail always makes two strong GetItems; ConsistentRead: true on every base-table read and never on GSI1; key-guard lookups return their not-found result without a call; health.ping is GetItem HEALTH/PING with ConsistentRead: true and abortSignal AbortSignal.timeout(2000).

Create dynamodb/index.ts: createDynamoRepositories(ctx, opts?: RepositoryOptions): Repositories with driver 'dynamodb', all 13 repositories bound to opts.now (default new Date().toISOString()), and close: async () => ctx.destroy(). In packages/backend/src/repositories/index.ts replace the FEAT-001 placeholder throw with the §3.3 dynamodb branch: log info 'Persistence driver: dynamodb' { table, region: config.aws.region, endpoint: endpoint ?? 'aws-default-chain' }, warn when the endpoint is set in production, then createDynamoRepositories(createDynamoContext({ region, endpoint, tableName })).

Create packages/backend/src/repositories/dynamodb/items.test.ts per the §8.3 row: alert round-trip, budgetEvidence, log GSI keys, audit/chat key formats, usage SK, ITEM_TOO_LARGE, entityType table over all 16 builders equal to ENTITY_TYPES, the exact emailLockItem shape, and [F34] a builder given an empty id throws INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Create packages/backend/src/repositories/dynamodb/commands.test.ts per the §8.3 row, with a recording fake { send: vi.fn(async (cmd) => ...) } that derives kind = cmd.constructor.name.replace(/Command$/, ''). Test code must NEVER spell QueryCommand, BatchGetCommand or BatchWriteCommand (AC19 gate). Cover: command shapes, entityType SET clauses, the lock Put, the ping ConsistentRead, error translation, two-page pagination (queryAll concat plus ExclusiveStartKey; queryCount 3+4 -> countActive 7; queryUpTo Limit/stop; services.all alertCount across pages; no GSI ConsistentRead), every upsertUser retry path with a logger.warn spy (ids only), findByEmail's two GetItems plus the mismatch warn, and the key guard (a 2,000-character id sends no command).

Add the dynamodb case to packages/backend/src/repositories/index.test.ts with a fresh-config dynamic import and DB_DRIVER=dynamodb, DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9. getRepositories().driver === 'dynamodb', and spies on node:http request and node:https request record zero calls.
Run the verification below and commit on dpi2, e.g. `feat(backend): DynamoDB single-table persistence driver`.

NOTES FOR LATER STEPS (FEAT-004 runs this driver against DynamoDB Local for the first time; until then it has only met the recording fake).
- Construction: createDynamoContext({ region, endpoint, tableName }) in dynamodb/client.ts returns { client, doc, tableName, destroy }. createDynamoRepositories(ctx, { now }) in dynamodb/index.ts returns driver 'dynamodb' and close -> ctx.destroy(). Repositories receive DynamoRepositoryContext = DynamoContext & { now } (exported from dynamodb/index.ts). Table tooling: APP_TABLE_GSI1 = 'GSI1' and buildCreateTableInput(tableName): CreateTableCommandInput in dynamodb/tableDefinition.ts (comment points at infra/lib/persistence-construct.ts; FEAT-005 adds the reverse comment). Send DescribeTable/CreateTable/DeleteTable/Scan via ctx.client with @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb commands; only Query/BatchGet/BatchWrite are gated.
- AC19 gate: PowerShell Select-String is case-insensitive, and the pattern also matches QueryCommandInput. Outside ops.ts never write those names in any case, even in comments or tests; use the exported type QueryInput from ops.ts, and the helpers queryAll/queryCount/queryUpTo/batchGetAll/batchWriteAll. ops.ts also exports send(ctx, command, op, { abortSignal?, handled? }) (names in handled are rethrown raw, unlogged), translateAwsError, unavailable(op, awsError), errorName, isConditionalCheckFailed, cancellationCodes, CONDITIONAL_CHECK_FAILED / TRANSACTION_CANCELED / TRANSACTION_CONFLICT, partitionQuery(pk, { filter, projection, names, values, descending }) (strong base-table Query with #pk/:pk) and mapLimit.
- Builders for the migration (items.ts): roleItem(RoleRow), userItem(UserRow; isActive = is_active === 1), emailLockItem(email, userId), preferencesItem({ userId, theme, widgetLayoutJson, updatedAt }), auditItem({ id, timestamp, actor, action, target, metadataJson, result, createdAt }), alertItem(alert, source, status, createdAt, { acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt } = nulls) (applies budgetEvidence), serviceItem(ServiceInput, source, createdAt), environmentItem({ id, name }, createdAt), logItem(log, source, alertId = null), metricItem(m, source, alertId = null), usageItem(u, source), analysisItem(AIAnalysisRecord, createdAt), integrationItem(IntegrationRow), chatSessionItem(ChatSession), chatMessageItem(ChatMessage), feedbackItem(ChatFeedback). Every builder checks every key attribute ([F34] -> INVALID_ARGUMENT) and the 380 KiB size guard (-> ITEM_TOO_LARGE). Mappers: itemToX for every entity; itemToAlert(item, { logIds, metricIds }).
- Stored shapes: logs, metrics and analyses carry alertId and GSI1PK ALERTLINK#<alertId> only while linked (attributes absent, not NULL, when unlinked; unlink REMOVEs both). Every other nullable field is written as NULL. A PREFS item created by preferences.update has only the attributes the patch supplied (+ userId, entityType, updatedAt). Messages logged: 'DynamoDB call failed' { op, awsError, requestId } (transient, warn), { op, awsError, hint } (fatal, error), { op, awsError } (unknown/other ValidationException, error); 'Alert evidence trimmed to fit DynamoDB item limit' { alertId, keptLines, droppedLines }; 'findByEmail: email lock does not match user' { userId }; 'upsertUser: user changed concurrently' { op, userId }; 'upsertUser: old email lock not owned by user' { userId, lockOwner }.
- Interpretation choices where the design text was not explicit (behaviour-preserving; please review): (1) linkLogsToAlert's BatchGet projects PK and SK, not only PK, because SK identifies which logs exist; log ids whose key cannot fit are dropped before the BatchGet (they can never have been stored). (2) replaceDerivedEvidence also applies the key guard: an id whose key cannot fit behaves like a missing alert ([] no-op, otherwise REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND), instead of a DynamoDB ValidationException (500). (3) aiAnalyses.insert treats any non-null alertId (including '') as a reference to check, so '' gives REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND like SQLite's foreign key. (4) The size guard runs in every builder, alertItem included (after the evidence budget). (5) Exhausted BatchGet/BatchWrite retries raise UNAVAILABLE with awsErrorName 'UnprocessedKeys' / 'UnprocessedItems'. (6) A TransactionCanceledException with a reason code other than None/ConditionalCheckFailed/TransactionConflict goes to translateAwsError's default row (rethrown unchanged, logged at error). (7) audit.query({ actor }) guards on fitsPartitionKey('ACTOR#' + actor).
- The registry statically imports the DynamoDB driver (design §3.3), so the SDK module loads in SQLite mode too; no client is constructed there. The new index.test.ts case uses DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9 and spies on http.request/https.request (default imports of node:http/node:https); it closes the repositories it builds.
- The MAIN workspace ' M .gitignore' observation recorded by FEAT-001 is still present; this step did not touch it.
